Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck and low back pain, consistent in nature
and severity with the mechanism of injury reported. Initial examination documented cervical and lumbar paraspinal tenderness,
restricted range of motion, and muscle guarding. Imaging and clinical findings clearly confirm soft tissue strain of the cervical
and lumbar regions. No prior injury to these body areas is known to this provider. Care was delivered over 27 visits, comprising
manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home program instruction. The course of treatment ran somewhat longer than typical
for uncomplicated strain injuries, refelcting a gradual but steady response to conservative care. Billing records reflect single,
non-duplicated charges for each service rendered. At discharge, the patient demonstrated improved range of motion and reduced
pain, with residual stiffness noted on forward flexion. Continued home exercise and as-needed follow-up were recommended.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
